subject.title: feat(ios): Siri App Intent integration — native "Hey Siri, ask OpenClaw..." support

question: Should first-party iOS Siri/App Intent execution be added, and if so should it route through paired-node identity/chat.send or node.event, or through a hardened /hooks/agent boundary?
rationale: The requested feature is aligned with iOS companion-app direction, but it adds a new voice/Shortcuts agent-execution surface where auth, session routing, local confirmation, reply delivery, and operator control are product and security choices rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve design-gated native intent
options.body: Implement the Siri/App Intent only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

options.title: Limit scope to Talk Mode launch
options.body: Treat the open Action Button/Talk Mode PR as the only first-party shortcut surface and leave parameterized Siri questions out of scope for now.

options.title: Keep webhook workaround external
options.body: Decline first-party Siri agent execution until there is stronger demand or a safer extension API, leaving Shortcuts plus webhook as the supported workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve design-gated native intent
recommendation.body: Implement the Siri/App Intent only after maintainers choose the auth boundary, session semantics, confirmation policy, and spoken-reply behavior, then require real iOS device proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest history signal for iOS Gateway/session boundaries and security-sensitive iOS routing decisions.
